qAndA.answer: The Splenius muscle group, which includes Splenius capitis and Splenius cervicis, is responsible for extending the head at the neck.
qAndA.question: Which muscle group is responsible for extending the head at the neck?

qAndA.answer: The Scalene muscles (anterior, middle, and posterior) elevate the ribs, assisting with inspiration or breathing in.
qAndA.question: What is the primary function of the Scalene muscles?

qAndA.answer: There are four infrahyoid muscles: Thyrohyoid, Omohyoid, Sternohyoid, and Sternothyroid.
qAndA.question: How many muscles make up the infrahyoid muscle group?

qAndA.answer: The Suprahyoid muscles are involved in depressing the mandible, allowing the jaw to open.
qAndA.question: Which muscle depresses the mandible to open the jaw?

qAndA.answer: The Middle Scalene muscle inserts into the first rib.
qAndA.question: What is the insertion point of the Middle Scalene muscle?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: In this video I will identify the axial muscles of the cervical region and
list the origin, insertion and action of major muscles in the cervical region.
We'll start getting oriented to the location of the superficial muscles in the
cervical region. The sternoclydo mastoid is a major muscle
response for the action of flexing or rotating the cervical vertebrae. To flex
the cervical vertebrae, to flex the head of the neck or if just one sternoclydo
mastoid contracts it will cause rotation of the cervical vertebrae to rotate
the head at the neck. The spleenous muscle group has an opposite action, the
spleenous muscles extend the cervical vertebrae to extend the head at the neck.
Then here we can see the middle scaling and anterior scaling. There are three
scaling muscles on each side and anterior middle and posterior scaling. The
posterior scaling is located just deep to the levator scapulee and so we
can't see it in this illustration. The action of the scaling is to elevate the
ribs. The other muscles we see here are levators scapulee and trapezius
are appendicular muscles and so we'll come back to them when we discuss the
muscles that position the pectoral girdle. Here with an anterior view zoomed in on
the muscles that are involved in positioning the hyoid bone and the
larynx or the voice box is positioned along with the hyoid bone by
muscles that insert onto the hyoid bone. The superhyoid muscles are muscles
located superior to the hyoid bone and have the action of elevating the
hyoid bone and larynx. This includes the geniohyoid digastric mylohyoid and
stylohyoid. In addition to elevating the hyoid bone in the larynx, geniohyoid
digastric and mylohyoid also have the action of depressing the mandible to open
the jaw. Then the infrahyoid muscles, the thyroid, umohyoid, sternohyoid and
sternothiroid, all have the action of depressing the hyoid bone and the larynx.
Now the sternoclidomastoid is a large superficial muscle in the cervical region
with its origin from the menugrium and the sternal end of the clavicle. Its
insertion is the mastoid process of the temporal bone and its action is to
flex or rotate the cervical vertebrae to flex or rotate the head at the neck.
Here with a posterior view we can see the splinius muscle group. There's splinius
capitis as well as splinius services. Together these muscles have the action of
extending the cervical vertebrae to extend the head at the neck.
Splinius capitis has its origin from the sphinus processes of cervical
vertebrae and inserts onto the temporal bone at the mastoid process to have
that action of extending the cervical vertebrae when both the right and the
left splinius contract or to rotate the cervical vertebrae to rotate the head
at the neck. If splinius capitis on the right side contracts it would rotate
the head to the right side and vice versa. Now here we see the middle scaling,
the middle scaling has its origin from the transverse processes of the
cervical vertebrae and its insertion into the first rib to have the action of
elevating the ribs which is an action that helps with breathing to assist in
expanding the thoracic cavity to draw air into the lungs during the act of
inspiration or breathing in. But the scaling's muscle group has three muscles on
each side of anterior, middle and posterior while both the anterior and middle
scaleings have their insertion onto the first rib the posterior scaling inserts
onto the second rib. So together the scaling's muscle group has an origin
from the transverse processes of cervical vertebrae and insertion onto ribs
one and two to have that action of elevating the ribs to assist with
inspiration drawing the air into the lungs.
